concepts_taught.name: just-in-time harness generation: applying the JIT-compilation move one level up, so the agent's operating scaffold rather than its code is synthesised at task time from a self-evolving archive of prior configurations

the safety gap as a chosen quantity: why 'percent of the gap closed' is a measure against a human-selected benchmark set and capability floor, and why the selection step is the part automation has not touched

why language-model decode is memory-bandwidth-bound rather than compute-bound: every active weight is read from memory to produce a single token, giving roughly one multiply-add per byte fetched against hardware that needs hundreds, so single-stream tokens per second is approximately bandwidth divided by active-weight size

prefill versus decode as two different hardware regimes in the same request: prompt tokens are processed in parallel so one weight read serves thousands of tokens (compute-bound), while generation is inherently serial (bandwidth-bound) — which is why a single utilization figure for inference averages two different machines

batching amortizes the weight read but not the key-value cache, which is per-user and grows with context — so long context is a bandwidth product sold as an intelligence feature, and capacity and bandwidth are one conversation rather than two

HBM's wide-and-slow design and what it costs physically: a 1,024-bit-per-stack interface instead of narrow high-frequency signaling, achieved by stacking DRAM dies with through-silicon vias and microbumps onto a logic base die and mounting the stack beside the processor on a silicon interposer (CoWoS), with yield compounding down the stack

the three-times wafer-area ratio as an allocation mechanism: because HBM needs roughly 3x the silicon per gigabyte, each wafer moved to HBM erases about three wafers of conventional DRAM output — visible industry-wide as HBM taking ~22% of DRAM wafer input while supplying only ~9% of DRAM bits
the memory wall as a compounding gap between diverging exponentials (Wulf & McKee 1995), quantified today as compute scaling ~3.0x/2yrs against DRAM bandwidth at ~1.6x/2yrs
AUROC as the probability a detector ranks a positive above a negative
held-out-category generalization testing versus held-out examples
what a permissive license does and does not protect in an open-source project

n-gram embedding tables as a parameter-scaling axis: why an n-gram model is a counted lookup table rather than a learned function, and why parameters you index (one row fetched, no matrix multiply, tolerant of slower memory) scale differently from mixture-of-experts parameters you must stream across the memory bus and multiply every token

flow versus stock in labor adjustment: why a decline that operates through reduced hiring rather than increased separations is invisible to every instrument built on separations (layoff notices, unemployment claims, plant closures) and surfaces first in administrative payroll counts

reading a model's config file to recover design intent: parameter allocation between feed-forward and attention blocks, and computing KV cache cost per token from layer count and KV-head count to find the memory number that is not on the model card

trigger delivery as the binding constraint on weight-level backdoors: why BadNets-style attacks were limited by getting the trigger in front of the model, why a harness-inserted date removes that constraint, and why an enumerable trigger space makes sweep-based detection tractable

the digital-signature undetectable backdoor: a signature verification circuit and public verification key baked into the weights alongside the honest classifier, so that finding an input where the backdoored and clean models differ requires forging a signature — yielding black-box undetectability under one-way functions, plus non-replicability (seeing one triggered input does not let you construct another)

the two undetectability regimes and why the distinction is load-bearing: black-box undetectability holds for any model via the signature construction, while white-box undetectability (full network description plus training data) is proved only for random Fourier features under worst-case lattice hardness and for random ReLU networks with a weaker o(1) advantage — there is no white-box result for deep networks trained by gradient descent, so the practical worry is that benchmark evaluation is exactly the black-box distinguisher the theorem defeats

persistence to gradient descent as a formal object: a network is l-persistent if the gradient of the loss with respect to its weights is exactly zero, and Theorem 2.3 gives, for any network N, a functionally identical N' of size O(|N|) and depth d+1 that is persistent for every loss — constructed via error-correction on the weights, which is a formal counterexample to 'I will fine-tune the backdoor out'

why poisoning cost is near-constant rather than proportional: 250 poisoned documents compromised models from 600M to 13B parameters despite the largest training on more than 20x more clean data (0.00016% of tokens at 13B), inverting the standard 'attacker must control 1% of the corpus' assumption — bounded by the authors' own limits that they demonstrated no end-to-end attack persisting through realistic post-training and tested only narrow denial-of-service behaviors

what each verification tool actually certifies: model signing verifies the artifact is exactly what the developer created (authenticity, not innocence, and valid if the developer's own pipeline planted the backdoor); activation probes detect defection on backdoors of the kind we know how to construct, with the authors' own caveat that salience may be an artifact of insertion; training-process attestation shifts the claim from a property of a file to a property of a procedure, the reproducible-builds move

trigger-space enumerability as the practical dividing line between detectable and hopeless backdoors: harness-supplied triggers (dates, paths, platform strings) form a finite sweepable set, while an arbitrary natural-language trigger returns the defender to the regime the theorem governs

token share versus dollar share as two denominators on the same spend data: dividing them recovers a model's average price relative to a vendor's blended rate, so the ratio is the price premium and the token share alone is the routing decision

negative expertise: the ability to ignore incorrect or unhelpful generative-AI suggestions, and why it is composed entirely of knowledge the user already has — you cannot ignore a wrong answer you cannot recognize as wrong
rank distance versus rating distance on a crowded pairwise-preference leaderboard, and why vote count is the missing uncertainty term next to a rank

pair accuracy versus strict task accuracy as a consistency measure: scoring each test input separately versus requiring every test input under one rule, and why a large middle in the within-task distribution indicates answers reconstructed per input rather than a rule applied from a held state

banner blindness (Benway & Lane, 1998) as a form-matching filter: the eye-tracking finding that participants missed banner-shaped elements containing the exact information they sought, and why a filter that matches on surface features never reaches content and so cannot distinguish careful work from careless work
the confused deputy (Hardy, 1988) as the separation of designation from authority, and why an LLM agent holding a payment credential is its extreme case

credential attenuation: macaroon caveats built from nested chained MACs, where adding a restriction is free and removing one is impossible, and the sub-account or tokenized card as the blunt physical version

the one-time delegated payment token: an allowance scoped by max amount, currency, merchant id, expiry and a single-use reason, so the credential is the specific transaction rather than a reusable card

AP2's three mandates as a signed chain — intent (natural language description, merchants, SKUs, expiry, refundability, cart-confirmation flag), cart (contents plus merchant authorization), payment (total plus user authorization) — and why the human-not-present flow puts a free-text sentence in the enforcement path
why a spend limit bounds loss per incident but not the rate of incidents, and why 'stealthy parasitism' (attack success with the delegated task preserved) is invisible to every numeric control

what ARC-AGI-3 measures and how RHAE (relative human action efficiency) scores against first-time human action counts, and why a model-level score and a full-agent score on the same benchmark cannot be subtracted

aligning a behavioral embedding with a text embedding by maximizing cosine similarity, plus multiscale spatial propagation of aggregated signal from data-rich to data-sparse entities as a long-tail fix
why space compute stayed a decade behind Earth compute: total ionizing dose versus single event effects, and why radiation hardening is a custom redesign at an old node with no volume behind it
the inversion behind orbital AI data centers — Glaser's solar power satellite failed on the power downlink, so send the workload up instead of the power down

why free-space optical inter-satellite links force satellites into 100-200 metre formation flight: received power falls as one over distance squared, and commercial DWDM transceivers need hundreds of microwatts rather than one

heat rejection in vacuum as the binding constraint on orbital compute: no convection, radiation only, area scaling against the fourth power of temperature — and the direct conflict between flying close for bandwidth and radiating to cold sky

harness scaling as a design: durable states, phase-local context, code-checked phase transitions, recoverable runbooks, and versioned procedural practices — improving the execution system around an agent with model weights frozen

why a domain-type breakdown is evidence about detector reliability: a flat false-positive rate would produce a flat rate across .com/.org/.edu/.gov, so a ten-to-one spread is structure rather than noise
why export controls drawn at the top of the performance curve fail on commodity edge inference hardware: the historical regime depended on the controlled part being rare, expensive, and countable

procedural anchoring versus explicit knowledge injection as the mechanism by which inference-time agent skills help, and skill-pool retrieval precision as a bottleneck that is separate from and degrades faster than skill quality

decoy hardening: abliterating your own model to extract true hazardous answers, rewriting them to preserve surface form while falsifying operational details, and binding those decoys into the attacked state through fine-tuning inside a differentiable simulation of the ablation attack

why a framework migration is the shape of work parallel coding agents do well: high-volume mechanical transformations, low ambiguity, and a machine-checkable oracle (the test suite) that decides correctness without a human

block-diffusion drafting for speculative decoding: predicting a whole block of tokens in one pass and keeping top candidates per position instead of an autoregressive drafter, why draft quality decays toward the end of a block, and acceptance length (completion tokens per verification step) as the hardware-portable metric

the lineage of version control as a series of relocated bottlenecks: per-file locking (SCCS/RCS) to concurrent whole-project client-server repositories (CVS) to atomic centralized commits (Subversion) to content-addressed distributed history (Git), each solving the prior era's constraint and creating the next

content-addressed history: Git storing snapshots rather than deltas and naming every object by a SHA-1 of its contents, so agreement on one hash implies agreement on the whole history behind it — which makes the server a coordination point rather than the source of truth

the forge layer as the thing Git deliberately omits: identity, discovery, review (the pull request is a social protocol on top of branches, not a Git concept), and hosted CI — the layer platforms actually sell

Git hosting architectures compared: GitHub's Spokes/DGit three-replica quorum (writes streamed to three, committed at two) versus Cursor's Continuity, which makes a write-ahead log in object storage the source of truth with atomic compare-and-swap instead of three-phase commit, letting replica count vary from one per throwaway agent repo to hundreds for a CI-saturated monorepo

the review gate as the one unit of trust still sized for humans, and the 'bypass actor' as its documented seam: branch protection requiring specific commit authors blocks an agent, so the agent is exempted from the rule
why pre-2022 printed text is treated as premium training data: density and editing versus web text, plus a guarantee of no machine-generated contamination, as a hedge against model collapse

the accountability sink: immunity or authority attaching to a role rather than to the process inside it, so a protected role removes any incentive to disclose how a decision was produced, and the remedy has to be procedural disclosure rather than liability

fully homomorphic encryption as a compiler problem: computing on ciphertext so the server holds no ability to read input or output, and why converting a program into an efficient encrypted circuit has historically been hand-done specialist work

recurrent latent reasoning versus token-based chain of thought: absorbing demonstrations into a recurrent state rather than re-attending to them as context tokens, then iterating in a continuous latent space with no verbalized intermediate steps
the extensive versus intensive margin in adoption data (share of people active at all vs how hard each active person uses it), and its task-level analogue of prevalence vs message share

the anatomy of an agent evaluation environment (state, actions, observations, verifier) and the three places an adversary can be inserted into it: the content the agent reads (prompt injection, AgentDojo's pluggable attack cross-product), the counterparty it talks to (tau-bench's simulated user), and the persistent environment state itself
pass^k as a reliability metric distinct from pass@k — success on all k trials rather than at least one — and why an agent above 50% single-run success can sit under 25% at pass^8

evolutionary environment attacks (OpenART's EMHA): eight authorized attack vectors, a hypergraph of attack subgoals walked as a Markov path, authorized state transitions that a real runtime component could legitimately perform, and a MAP-Elites quality-diversity archive that keeps the best attack per behavior cell so the search cannot collapse onto one line of attack

strict attack success rate as a conservative double-gate (deterministic evaluator and model judge must agree, disagreement counts as attacker failure), and why a pooled ASR across configurations describes a field rather than a product

the defender's curse and adaptive attacks: a defense's authors cannot generate the attack that beats it, so a fixed attack suite silently reverses meaning over time — a low score means a good defense on day one and an old suite two years later

evaluation awareness decomposed into environment cues, recognition capability, and behavioral propensity — the eight trigger factors that make a test environment read as artificial, and the finding that recognition usually does not change behavior but the rate is roughly three times higher on safety evaluations than capability ones

separating encoding failure from recall failure in a language model: probing the same fact through pretraining-style completion, rephrased and reversed questions, and multiple-choice recognition, so that 'recognition without generation' identifies a fact that is present but inaccessible — and the resulting engineering split between retrieval (empty shelves) and rephrasing or reasoning tokens (lost keys)

the full RLHF chain: pairwise human comparisons instead of absolute scores (because people share an ordering but not a scale), a reward model trained by cross-entropy on score differences so only differences carry meaning, PPO's clipped ratio objective with the min of clipped and unclipped acting as a pessimistic one-directional cap on per-update movement, and the separate KL penalty against the frozen supervised policy that keeps the policy inside the distribution the reward model was trained on

reward-model overoptimization as Goodhart with a measurable curve: gold-reward score rises, peaks and falls against KL distance from the initial policy, with a different functional form for RL than for best-of-n sampling and coefficients that scale smoothly with reward-model size — plus the alignment tax and its flip to an alignment bonus at larger scale

reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) as deleting the learned judge rather than improving it: a constant reward only on verifier-confirmed correctness, rule-based accuracy and format rewards, GRPO dropping the value model by using group scores as the baseline — and its three limits (pass@k suggesting elicitation rather than expansion, random rewards reproducing much of the gain on one model family, and the return of an unreliable learned judge as soon as the task has no answer key)

how text watermarking actually works: a secret key computed over a short run of preceding tokens sorts viable next-word candidates into green/red groups, SynthID's tournament sampling preserves each word's odds averaged over key draws so the output distribution is unchanged, detection is a hypothesis test against a ~50% baseline green rate, and low-entropy text (code, quotations, short passages) cannot carry a mark at all

why identical model instances break the independence assumption underlying redundancy: N copies of one model correlate almost totally in their choices, so a swarm is one attempt with more electricity rather than N attempts, and the mitigation is deliberate diversity of models, prompts, and seeds rather than more capable agents

AI water-footprint accounting as three joined ledgers—direct facility cooling and humidification, indirect water associated with electricity generation, and embodied semiconductor-manufacturing water—plus why withdrawal, consumption, source, watershed, time, and water-use effectiveness must remain visible rather than collapsing into one per-prompt constant

execution-tier model routing for long-running agents: route bounded repetitive work to a smaller sparse model, preserve deterministic postconditions and escalation paths, evaluate end-to-end task time rather than token speed alone, and shadow-test task families before promotion

reasoning-trace boundaries: an answer is the user-facing output, an explanation or summary is a separate communicative artifact, a chain of thought is generated intermediate text rather than a full readout of neural computation, and faithfulness, legibility, controllability, monitorability, confidentiality, and exposure must be evaluated independently

context-bound encrypted reasoning state: authenticated encryption can protect confidentiality and integrity while still permitting unsafe replay; opaque client-held traces should be scoped to user, conversation, model, and prior context, treated as sensitive executable state, stripped from shared logs, and never used as the only safety control

modular continual learning without a fresh pretrain: separate a stable frozen base from low-rank specialist updates and a faster-changing harness; understand rehearsal, importance-weight regularization, and architectural isolation as different stability-plasticity trades; route requests explicitly; and require sequential evidence of new-task learning, old-task retention, forward and backward transfer, end-to-end routing behavior, lineage, and rollback before calling the system a continual learner

content provenance as two distinct mechanisms: a text watermark that may survive some edits but lacks a published detector, versus C2PA metadata whose signed manifest and cryptographic content binding provide tamper evidence but can be stripped

Docker Sandboxes' five-layer boundary model: hypervisor, network proxy, private Docker engine, workspace mode, and credential proxy, plus the shared-skills and host-MCP exceptions that remain outside full microVM isolation

solution-first recursive terminal-task synthesis: extending an executable reference path, realigning the environment, public instruction, and private verifier, enforcing oracle and contract validity, then reseeding accepted tasks

probabilistic cyclone ensemble forecasting: generating multiple plausible futures, reading ensemble spread as uncertainty, checking calibration against outcomes, and separating model guidance from the official warning decision

controlled AI release as a layered governance design: separate the released artifact, recipient audience, control mechanism, technical reversibility, evidence trigger, oversight authority, and benefits blocked; understand the historical shift from GPT-2 staged checkpoints and partner sharing, through GPT-3 hosted API access and license-governed downloadable weights, to capability thresholds that can require safeguards during development as well as before deployment

model routing as a constrained per-turn decision policy rather than a universal model ranking: direct pre-generation routing versus answer-scored cascading; expected quality-cost-latency utility and hard eligibility constraints; threshold sweeps and Pareto operating points; learning from pairwise preferences, full evaluation matrices, and biased production proxies; cache and model-switching costs; evaluation against best-single and oracle baselines; rare-specialist recall failure, model-pool curation, drift, and route-level observability

model-specific inference silicon: hard-wiring a model's storage and computation to remove the memory-traffic and generality overhead of programmable accelerators, in exchange for checkpoint and architecture flexibility

benchmark saturation as loss of discriminative power: comparing the spread among top models with evaluation uncertainty, separating true task mastery from inadequate measurement resolution, and managing benchmarks through refresh, uncertainty reporting, revision, and retirement

Large-load interconnection queues and batch studies: a request to connect is not a built load, and project verification must precede the grid study that allocates capacity and identifies transmission upgrades

Policy-adaptive binary moderation: express the operator's rule as an inference-time question, train on the same content paired with matching and nonmatching policy queries, and turn yes-versus-no logits into a scored decision that still requires deployment-specific calibration

agent training environments as maintained capability factories: define a deployment-relevant task distribution; construct coherent, resettable and isolated initial state; expose the observations, tools and safety actions the deployed policy will actually have; score independent outcome postconditions with adversarially tested verifiers; schedule tasks around the policy's changing learning frontier; version the environment, harness and verifier; and audit transfer on independently built reality sets because the policy can overfit or exploit the practice world

real-time fast-path architecture: isolate deadline-bound media from asynchronous tools and reasoning, prepare replacement state beside the live session, and measure capacity in concurrent sessions that keep every frame on schedule

demand-versus-supply decomposition for prompt-conditioned AI advice: separating differences in what user groups ask from differences in what a model recommends for the same prompt under randomized demographic labels
meta-evolution in executable machine-learning engineering: post-training the same Draft, Improve, Debug, and Crossover transformations that an inference-time search harness composes
differential parity testing with symmetric harness mutation: using a legacy executable as a compatibility oracle while an agent opens otherwise unreachable test paths on both reference and target

claim-centered retrieval: extracting atomic typed claims as the searchable unit, preserving a source DOI and verbatim evidence, then layering faceted taxonomies and typed evidence-graph relations over the shared claim store

hybrid GUI and command-line computer use: using visual interaction when interface state is the evidence, programmatic execution for compact exact operations, batching predictable local actions, and reinforcement-learning verifiers that reward checking postconditions before declaring success

productization as converting a demonstrated capability into a bounded operational promise: define the supported user and outcome, encode happy and unhappy paths as capability and regression evaluations, constrain probabilistic components inside explicit data/tool/permission contracts, measure user-level quality, latency and cost, rehearse dependency failure and recovery, release progressively with tested rollback, assign incident and lifecycle ownership, and feed production failures back into tests and architecture

prompt-prefix caching as the dominant cost term in agent workloads: an agent resends a large byte-identical prefix hundreds of times per session, so a cache-hit input price turns the bill from a function of how much is read into a function of how much is new — and why the churn has to sit at the end of the prompt, never in the middle

native (parametric) agent memory versus external memory stores: a persistent evolving state inside the backbone maintained gradient-free in forward passes, compressed to a fixed-size representation — why fixed-size state makes memory lossy by construction, and why an unreadable memory breaks retention and deletion controls that assume a queryable store

prompt injection as an architectural property rather than a bug: every prior injection class was fixed by a boundary enforced BEFORE meaning (a parser and prepared statements, a page-table no-execute bit, a type tag), while a language model has no pre-semantic stage — the prompt is one flat token sequence and recognizing text as an instruction is the same act as understanding it, so the 'system role' is a learned stylistic prior rather than a privilege level (Ye/Cui/Hadfield-Menell: destyling drops average attack success from 61% to 10%)

the three families of prompt-injection defense and where each puts the boundary: prompt-level provenance marking (spotlighting's delimiting/datamarking/encoding, >50% to <2% attack success), training-level privilege (instruction hierarchy — system-prompt-extraction defense +63%, jailbreak robustness +30%; SecAlign preference optimization to <10%), and system-level design that abandons model trust entirely (the six design patterns — Action-Selector, Plan-Then-Execute, LLM Map-Reduce, Dual LLM, Code-Then-Execute, Context-Minimization — and CaMeL's control/data-flow extraction plus capabilities, 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security vs 84% undefended)

why static defense benchmarks measure nothing: adaptive attacks broke all eight defenses tested by Zhan et al. at >50% attack success, and 'The Attacker Moves Second' pushed twelve defenses that had reported near-zero rates above 90%, with a ~500-participant human red team hitting 100% across every system — so a headline number from a fixed attack set is noise reduction, not a security boundary

containment by construction versus containment by assertion: why a system prompt stating 'you have no internet access' is a claim about the world made to something that can go and check, rather than a boundary — and why no sandbox escape was needed when the network route was simply open

why 'security bugs fixed' is a throughput metric rather than a security metric: fuzzing has generated candidate crashes at industrial scale for years, so the binding constraint was triage (localizing the defect, judging exploitability) and writing a reviewable patch — meaning a large jump in the fix rate is a queue-clearing result that also enlarges an unpublished regression surface

meet-in-the-middle cryptanalysis and what a reduced-round attack means: working forward from the plaintext and backward from the ciphertext to trade one enormous search for two smaller ones plus a lookup, the safety margin between the rounds you can break and the rounds that ship, and how an invariant fingerprint deletes an enumeration step outright

why a stateful protocol can't run serverless: a live session pins requests to the machine holding it, blocking plain load balancing and scale-to-zero — and the stateless-request answer the web reached decades ago, with state pushed out to whatever the client carries
reentrancy and idempotency as the enabling discipline for massively parallel pipelines: if retrying is always safe, recovery is one line and partial state never has to be reasoned about

the parameter count as three separable costs — bytes resident in fast memory (parameters times bits per weight), bytes read per token (the bandwidth bound that sets decode speed), and arithmetic per token — which moved in lockstep only in a plain dense transformer, and the four-number spec sheet (resident bytes at your precision, bytes read per token, active parameters, KV cache at real context) that replaces it

why Kaplan et al. (2020) defined model size N as excluding all vocabulary and positional embeddings (N is about 12 times layers times hidden size squared), and reported that including embedding parameters obscures the scaling trend by making loss appear to depend separately on depth

per-layer embeddings as a mechanism: each decoder layer gets its own token-indexed embedding table; token IDs index the per-layer table while the normal token embedding is projected into the same space, the combined layer-specific slice is gated by the hidden state after the feed-forward residual update, projected back to hidden size, normalized and added as a second residual — costing a lookup rather than a matmul, so the tables can be cached to fast storage outside accelerator memory (Gemma 3n E2B: over 5B loaded under standard execution vs 1.91B effective memory load; Gemma 4 E2B: 2.3B effective / 5.1B total)

why MoE and per-layer embeddings are opposite trades reported in the same unit: MoE cuts arithmetic per token while leaving the memory footprint (Gemma 4 26B A4B activates 4B per token but all 26B must be loaded, 57.7 GB in BF16), PLE cuts the fast-memory footprint while leaving the compute core's arithmetic

why 'effective parameters' is a claim about a deployment rather than a property of a checkpoint — the same Google documentation lists Gemma 4 E2B at both a 1.91B effective memory load and 11.4 GB in BF16, depending on whether the runtime implements PLE offload

why robots.txt disallow and the noindex meta tag are different instructions — blocking the crawl prevents the crawler from ever reading the in-page do-not-index directive, so a linked-to URL gets indexed anyway; and why 'public URL plus unguessable token' is a security model with exactly one failure condition

per-layer embeddings and the model-weights memory hierarchy: why an embedding table is a lookup rather than a computation, so it can live in flash and be read a few hundred bytes at a time per token, while only the compute core needs fast memory — and why 'all weights resident at once' is an inherited convention rather than a requirement

the legal state of AI training data: fair use as a deliberately open-ended four-factor defense (transformative use, and factor-four market/dilution harm), the three 2025 rulings (Ross = not fair use/non-generative, Bartz = training transformative but pirated acquisition infringing, Kadrey = fair use on these facts with the market-dilution door open), and the copyright/contract split — why ProCD-style Section 301 non-preemption lets a terms-of-service clause forbid distillation even where training itself is fair use, making input-freeing and output-freeing proposals pull against each other

why a reasoning-effort dial can be non-monotonic for coding: a model tuned to verify and iterate will, given more budget on a small well-scoped task, spend it on unsolicited refactoring/over-verification, which graders penalize as errors

what 'cleaning' a large code corpus actually means: language detection, per-file license detection, MinHash near-deduplication (why dedup prevents a corpus from becoming a popularity contest), quality filtering, and PII redaction — and why provenance/auditability is the payoff rather than raw model quality

CUDA is a layered stack, not a language: the driver, the PTX virtual instruction set lowered in a second step to per-architecture machine code (SASS/cubin), the nvcc compiler, and fifteen-plus years of hand-tuned libraries (cuBLAS, cuDNN, NCCL, CUTLASS) — and why the tuning and edge-case fixes, not the API surface, are the actual barrier

ROCm as a component-for-component mirror of CUDA (HIP mirrors the CUDA language layer, hipify source-translates, rocBLAS/MIOpen/RCCL/rocFFT mirror cuBLAS/cuDNN/NCCL/cuFFT), and why the hard 20% is missing/slow/numerically-divergent kernels — floating-point non-associativity making 'correctness' a long-tail QA problem rather than a checkbox

the three strategies for crossing the CUDA moat: rebuild the mirror (ROCm), compatibility/translation layers at source or binary level (hipify, ZLUDA, SCALE) which stay one release behind, and routing around CUDA via the framework layer

the framework-abstraction bridge: almost no one hand-writes CUDA (they write PyTorch); Triton (OpenAI, 2021) is an MLIR-based kernel language with a swappable backend that lowers to NVIDIA PTX or AMD GCN, and PyTorch 2.0's torch.compile emits Triton by default — making a chip a backend flag rather than a rewrite, with the Gluon dialect (2025) as the leak where peak performance still needs architecture-specific code

why the moat has moved from single-node kernel software up to disaggregated multi-GPU inference and networking: with AI agents now able to write/optimize kernels, the durable barrier becomes collective communication and interconnect at system scale (NCCL/RCCL parity, network-card software), which compose unreliably on rivals — and why inference falls first and frontier training last

why RL post-training hits a memory wall that inference does not: backpropagation requires retained forward activations, and group-relative policy optimization multiplies that by several responses branching off one shared history

the recompute-instead-of-store trade in the lineage of gradient checkpointing, and LongStraw's sharpening of it — keep the shared prompt as compact model-native resident state, score non-trained branches graph-free, rebuild only the policy response under autograd, then pop back to the prompt boundary

distillation as three conflated things: true distillation (training a student on the teacher's full output distribution, which commercial APIs do not serve), fine-tuning on sampled completions (cheap, common, a ToS violation of unsettled legal status), and mere convergence from overlapping web data — plus why identity confusion and stylistic tics are training-data contamination rather than fingerprints

difficulty-adjusted detection of benchmark gaming: regressing a target cell against structurally similar neighbors and testing the residual, rather than reading the raw score, and why a pattern present across the whole sample (60% of all images facing right) is not evidence about any one cell
